subject: MSA/Order Form: allocation of fines and 3rd-party claims
body:
From: marta.gomez@finsecure.com
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.example.com
Cc: james.liu@finsecure.com; erin.cho@finsecure.com
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed redlines to MSA re: regulatory fines and 3P claims

Hannah —

Thanks again for sending the draft MSA and order form. Our legal team returned with a handful of substantive asks focused on Limitation of Liability. High level: FinSecure cannot accept a general cap that would effectively waive our responsibility for regulatory fines (GDPR/CCPA/PCI) or shift third-party penalties to customers. Proposed changes attached (FinSecure_MSA_Redline_v3.pdf).

Key ask: carve out regulatory fines and statutory penalties from the cap; unlimited liability for those amounts. Also proposed language requiring Redwood to indemnify FinSecure for third-party regulatory claims and PCI assessment penalties where Redwood's processing caused the event.

We recognize this is a sensitive area — happy to set up a call to walk through specifics.

Best,
Marta Gomez
Head of Legal Operations
FinSecure Inc.

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.example.com
To: marta.gomez@finsecure.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.example.com; priyom_das@redwood.example.com; kimberly_park@redwood.example.com
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed redlines to MSA re: regulatory fines and 3P claims

Marta —

Thanks for the redlines and for calling out the compliance concerns. Looping in Aditya (legal) and Priyom (sales) so we can respond with a proposed middle ground. We want to be fair — protecting customers is important — but we also need predictable exposure on our end so we can price and underwrite Dedicated / Private deployments.

Action plan: Aditya, can you review the FinSecure edits and indicate which of their carve-outs we can accept, which require insurance/insured sublimits, and which we need to push back on? Priyom, I think the customer will prioritize a clear remedy and operational commitments (SOC2, PCI evidence).

I'll suggest a quick 30-minute sync tomorrow after you review.

Thanks,
Hannah
Senior Manager, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: aditya_rao@redwood.example.com
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.example.com; priyom_das@redwood.example.com; kimberly_park@redwood.example.com
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 13:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed redlines to MSA re: regulatory fines and 3P claims

Team —

I reviewed FinSecure_MSA_Redline_v3.pdf. High level comments below (short form):

1) Regulatory fines carve-out: We cannot accept an unlimited carve-out for regulatory penalties. Market practice (and our carrier/underwriting constraints) requires either a limited carve-out tied to the Order Form value or an insured sublimit + cooperation/defense obligations.

2) Suggested compromise: carve out statutory fines up to a defined sublimit equal to 2x the annual committed fees under the Order Form for the affected service, but require Redwood to maintain appropriate cyber/privacy insurance and to use commercially reasonable efforts to defend/mitigate. For amounts above that sublimit, parties would use mutual indemnity subject to a joint defense and mitigation ladder.

3) Third-party claims (PCI/processor penalties): We can accept indemnity for direct damages caused by Redwood's breach of our obligations (e.g., security or data processing failures), but we should exclude consequential damages and limit total exposure (cap) to a multiple of fees. We should not accept unlimited third-party indemnity without attaching the customer's procurement obligations (e.g., notification, timely investigation access, control of defense for Redwood-originated claims).

4) Evidence/security posture: we should provide FinSecure SOC2 + PCI scope statements and offer an audit provision (redacted) and a commitment to cooperate with regulator requests; those operational commitments will ease their concern and may reduce their insistence on unlimited caps.

5) Practical negotiation approach: propose a structured clause that (a) lists regulatory fines as an excluded category up to sublimit X, (b) requires Redwood to carry insurance and cooperate, and (c) ties any excess to a mutual indemnity with defined caps and conditions. Offer a 30-day remediation cure window for incidents that are remediable.

I can draft redline language for the MSA and a cover email to propose the compromise.

- Aditya
Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

---

From: priyom_das@redwood.example.com
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.example.com; aditya_rao@redwood.example.com; marta.gomez@finsecure.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.example.com
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Proposed redlines to MSA re: regulatory fines and 3P claims

Marta —

Really appreciate the clarity from your team. We want to be fast and pragmatic here. From a commercial perspective FinSecure is a strategic target — Redwood is prepared to offer the following:

- Carve-out for regulatory fines up to the greater of (i) the Order Form committed fees for the 12 months following the incident or (ii) $1M; Redwood will also maintain cyber/privacy insurance with a $5M aggregate limit.
- For third-party PCI/assessment penalties caused by Redwood, Redwood will indemnify FinSecure subject to (i) Redwood having control of the defense where Redwood’s systems are implicated, (ii) notification and cooperation obligations by FinSecure, and (iii) a cap equal to 3x the Order Form annual committed fees.
- We will provide SOC2 attestation and a redacted PCI report and are willing to include a 30-day remediation cure for certain security issues.

If that is acceptable, Hannah and I can put calendar time on both sides to finalize language and aim to close before the end of next week.

Thanks,
Priyom
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: OrderForm_FinSecure_v1.xlsx; SOC2_Attestation_2025.pdf

From: marta.gomez@finsecure.com

Cc: james.liu@finsecure.com; erin.cho@finsecure.com
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 12:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed redlines to MSA re: regulatory fines and 3P claims

Priyom/Hannah —

Thanks for the quick response and for the insurance commitment. A couple items from our side:

- The proposed $1M floor is acceptable as long as we get clear remediation commitments and a guarantee that Redwood will not block our right to cooperate with regulators.
- For third-party PCI penalties: we need explicit language that Redwood will cover fines and assessments directly tied to Redwood’s processing failures (including scope for forensic costs and reasonable PCI assessor fees).
- We will need to route any final redline through our CISO and procurement; can Redwood provide a single point of contact for technical evidence requests (Erin CC'd is our operational lead).

Can we do a call Monday 10/5 at 10am PT to go through the proposed clause line-by-line?

Best,
Marta

Kimberly — can you prep certified SOC2 summary and a contact for PCI evidence requests ahead of the call.

Goal for the call: agree on a single compromise paragraph that allows both sides to proceed to Order Form signature this month.

Hannah
